messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: prod-west inference fleet — latency p95 increased ~3x starting ~2026-03-15T02:00Z. Auto-alert: p95 > 600ms for 15m. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC12345

Alice N.: acked. I'm oncall for this slot, grabbing timeline and impact. tagging infra and eng-runtime.

Bharat P.: +1, here if you want me to takeover after first triage.

Alice N.: quick checks:
- rolling up last deploys: nothing pushed in last 6h except a kernel/security patch to prod-west nodes at 01:45Z via infra autopilot.
- traffic shape: traffic stable, QPS steady.
- fallback routes engaged automatically for some routes earlier (logs show 01:58Z).

Sophia C.: customer-impact: alerting shows ~12 customers experienced >2x latency. 3 customers hit SLO p95 > 1s. CS/SE notified.

Alice N.: attaching initial span sample (from sleuth traces) — short snippet:
```
span_id=0xabc123 trace=0xfeeddead service=inference runtime=server-3
span: decode_tokens 2ms
span: KV_cache_lookup 120ms
span: attention_kv_dispatch 480ms
span: kernel_syscall_wait 320ms
```

Lucas M.: attention_kv_dispatch ballooning. We normally see that at ~20-30ms, not hundreds. Any kernel info?

infra-bot: kernel updates executed on nodes:
- 01:45Z: kernel 6.1.0-1 -> 6.1.0-5 (backported micropatches) applied to group prod-west-a (60 hosts)
- 02:10Z: rollout paused on failures in prod-west-b (20 hosts)
- Auto-rollback not triggered.

Bharat P.: hypothesis 1: kernel change introduced scheduler/irq/preempt behaviour that increases syscall latencies under high ephemeral thread counts (inference runtime uses many short-lived worker threads). Hypothesis 2: moved cpufreq governor causing turbo/thermal interplay -> longer syscall wait.

Alice N.: reproducing perf counters on an affected node (selected host id=server-3):
```
# perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations,cycles,instructions -p <pid> sleep 30
  12,345 context-switches
  5,600 cpu-migrations  <-- high compared to baseline 300
  8.2B cycles
  3.9B instructions
```

Sophia C.: customer timeline notes: first complaints at 02:03Z, automated retries began 02:05Z, some requests timed out at 02:07–02:15Z.

Lucas M.: I pulled `dmesg` from server-3:
```
[01:46:12] kernel: BUG: preempt not balancing? scheduling latency detected
[01:46:13] kernel: perf: interrupt took 1000+ us
```

Alice N.: mitigation attempt 1 (02:25Z): throttled batch size for some routes to reduce worker churn. Immediate p95 drop from ~900ms -> ~700ms, but still above threshold.

Bharat P.: mitigation attempt 2 (02:40Z): rolled back kernel on a canary subset (10 hosts) to 6.1.0-1. On those hosts p95 returned to baseline ~180ms within 3 mins.

Alice N.: validated: canary rollback produced clear improvement. Rolling back remaining prod-west-a hosts in waves now. Progress: 30/60 hosts rolled back at 02:55Z.

infra-bot: rollback job status:
- rolled-back: 30 hosts (success)
- in-progress: 20 hosts
- failed: 10 hosts (OOM during rollback agent, investigating)

Sophia C.: impact update to CS sent at 02:58Z. Estimated affected customers now 4 steady; most recovered after rollback.

Lucas M.: digging into traces, we see kernel_syscall_wait span correlates with cpu_migrations and softirq spikes. I'm attaching a short trace flame: (inline simplified)
```
--root--
  kv_lookup 120ms
  attention_kv_dispatch 480ms
    -> blocked on syscall 320ms
```

Alice N.: next actions in-thread:
- collect full perf counters, ftrace and eBPF snapshots from one bad host and one rolled-back host (Bharat)
- preserve /var/log/redwood/inference and dmesg from 01:30Z–03:30Z and upload to s3://redwood-incident/2698765432/
- assign RCA owner and kernel contact

Bharat P.: I'm taking RCA lead for this thread. Kernel team pinged (cc @kernel-team). I'll own collection and vendor escalation.

Sophia C.: customer follow-up: a short status note went out at 03:05Z. We should prepare a post-incident timeline and impact table once we have final rollbacks.

Alice N.: logs to collect (commands):
```
sudo tar czf /tmp/incident-2698765432-logs.tgz /var/log/redwood/inference/*.log /var/log/messages /var/log/kern.log
sudo perf record -a -o /tmp/perf-$(hostname).data sleep 60
sudo bpftool prog list > /tmp/bpf-progs.txt
sudo cat /proc/version > /tmp/kernel-version.txt
```
Please upload to s3 with `aws s3 cp` and post the object links here.

Lucas M.: running `perf` on a healthy (rolled-back) host now — baseline cpu_migrations under same workload: ~280, context-switches ~3,200. Attaching perf script diff in thread.

infra-bot: note: some rollback agents failed due to disk pressure. Operators increasing ephemeral scratch in those hosts.

Alice N.: customer impact quick table (preliminary):
- total requests impacted: ~9.4K across 00:58–03:10Z
- SLO breaches: 3 customers (p95 > 1s) for ~40m each
- revenue-sensitive customers: 2 flagged, customer SEs notified

Bharat P.: notes from kernel-team meeting: possible regression in scheduler path introduced by micropatch handling of irq-affinity. Kernel team requested eBPF traces showing softirq distribution.

Sophia C.: action: I'll create a concise Incident Postmortem doc skeleton and link once RCA artifacts are uploaded.

Alice N.: For the in-thread hypothesis tracker (quick):
- H1 (kernel scheduling regression) — evidence: dmesg warnings, perf cpu_migrations spike, canary rollback success. Confidence: high
- H2 (runtime regression / recent deploy) — evidence: none (no code deploys). Confidence: low
- H3 (hardware/thermal) — evidence: partial (some hosts show higher temperature spikes), but rollout correlation stronger for patched hosts. Confidence: medium-low

Lucas M.: assigning tasks:
- Bharat: lead RCA + kernel contact + upload eBPF traces
- Alice: timeline + centralize traces + ops coordination for remaining rollbacks
- Sophia: customer comms + postmortem draft
- Lucas: perf/tracing analysis and correlation

Bharat P.: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-incident/2698765432/server-3-perf.data, server-3-dmesg.txt, server-3-ebpf.txt (links) — sharing snapshot at 03:40Z.

Alice N.: thanks — confirming I can reproduce the lower-latency behavior on rolled-back images. Logging this thread as primary source for RCA timeline.

infra-bot: incident state changed -> mitigation in progress (03:50Z).

Sophia C.: rough ETA for postmortem first draft: 2026-03-15T08:00Z (4hrs) after artifact review. Will attach impact numbers and customer comm history.

Alice N.: closing loop for now — remaining work: finish rollbacks, reconcile failed agents, deep dive kernel traces. We'll follow up with formal RCA doc. If new pages occur, re-open thread. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to SEV-2 at 03:55Z — mitigations working, partial rollback successful.

Bharat P.: handing off final followups to next oncall @Alice (end of shift note). I'll continue with kernel-team sync offline.

Alice N.: acknowledged handoff. Thanks team.
